evidence.interpretation: These replay-fit and OOF residual diagnostics motivate testing estimator variance; resident replay trained the body and is herded, so neither is independent old-population generalization evidence. Direct-mode diagnostics do not establish a chained-mode failure.

hypothesis: A modest increase in the existing identity-slope penalty can reduce variance in weakly identified affine directions. Adjacent chained representations are expected to be closer than initial-anchor and later representations, making the identity prior plausible but not guaranteed correct. Higher gamma may instead introduce harmful bias.
mathematical_basis: After weighted centering, A_gamma-I=(U_c^T W U_c+gamma I)^-1 U_c^T W (V_c-U_c), b=mean_v-mean_u A_gamma. Increasing gamma damps poorly identified deviations from identity. With d=768, early five-fold fits can contain fewer resident rows than the affine coefficient dimension; existing gamma already regularizes them, and the candidate only strengthens it.
unchanged: All other body training, data, replay, estimator, head and validation settings are identical to the original chained screen. No formal test information is used.
execution: Start fresh analytic moments; reuse only the guarded unchanged CE body trajectory. Never resume a gamma=.01 analytic checkpoint under gamma=.1.
expected_observations: Compare three-stage training-holdout Final/AIA/old-class accuracy to the parent chained screen.
Inspect OOF residual covariance trace, map replay fit and PSD diagnostics; a lower residual trace alone is not sufficient for selection.
Only a surviving candidate can be extended unchanged through all ten development stages before final selection.
search_scope: One ImageNet-R candidate; no grid and no other candidate created by this decision.
